holidays.name: World Coconut Day
holidays.description: A tropical party for one of nature's most useful foods. Coconuts give us water, milk, oil, flour, and shells that can be turned into bowls. Today is a good day to crack one open, sip the water, and thank the palm tree.
holidays.origin: The Asian and Pacific Coconut Community (APCC) started the observance in 2009. It falls on September 2 to mark the anniversary of the group's founding in 1969.
holidays.funFact: Botanically, a coconut is a drupe, which makes it a relative of peaches and cherries. It isn't a true nut.

holidays.name: Pierce Your Ears Day
holidays.description: A day for people who have been thinking about getting their ears pierced. If you've wanted a new stud or hoop, this is the nudge to go and get it done. Just use a professional piercer.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on quirky holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Ötzi the Iceman, a mummy about 5,300 years old, had stretched earlobes. Ear piercing is one of the oldest known forms of body modification.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Popsicle Day
holidays.description: A salute to the frozen, fruity treat that turns your tongue a suspicious shade of blue. It's a good day to grab one, or to freeze your own from blended blueberries.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It lands in the last warm days of summer, when frozen treats are still welcome.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries are one of the few naturally blue foods. Their color comes from anthocyanin pigments, and the same pigments can tint your tongue and lips.
